note: One word with the delimiter, reverse and the six orders. Strings are compared by code point (not by locale), numeric reads a decimal at the start of the line without an exponent, IP address puts text that is not four decimal fields of 0 to 255 after the addresses in code point order, and the sort is stable.
A uniform Fisher-Yates shuffle on the host's cryptographic random generator (+random); the delimiter is a choice from the shared list.
Keeps the first of each in place. With show-count each line is written as its count, a space and the line, in the order of first appearance.
Keeps the lines where the regular expression matches, or with invert the others. Regex flags i, m and s can be given; the pattern is a Forge regex parameter (always the u flag).
A negative number keeps all but the last |number| lines, as in CyberChef.
A negative number keeps all but the first |number| lines. A number of 0 keeps none (CyberChef returns everything for 0).
The number right-aligned to the width of the longest number (CyberChef sizes it by the line count, which is the same with offset 0), a space, the line. The delimiter is a choice.

Works line by line with the same pattern (up to 5 spaces or tabs, digits, separators). CyberChef lets the separator class match line feeds, so a line holding only a number swallows the line break; Forge never joins lines.
Start or end, length and padding text, counted in code points; a padding of several characters is repeated and cut like padStart.
Cuts each line into pieces of at most the width in characters (code points), counting characters and not words; empty lines stay.

ASCII box and Markdown pipe table; the HTML format is dropped (Forge shows text only). The cell and row delimiters are choices from the shared list rather than free text, and a double-quoted cell may hold the cell delimiter (not a row delimiter). The ASCII box has a rule after every row, with = under the header row.

Plain text instead of HTML: a unified-style diff by line (headers, hunks, context lines), and by word or character the second sample's text with [-deleted-] and {+inserted+} marks. Myers' shortest difference; ignore whitespace; the sentence, CSS and JSON modes, and the show added, removed and subtraction switches, are dropped.
A tree in the style of the tree command with plain characters (|-- and `--), a root line of a dot, siblings in code point order. The path separator and the delimiter between paths are parameters.
